title: Emrys and the Colony
premise: Ada Okonkwo has spent a decade flying dead-drop cargo runs through contested orbits, keeping her ship, her crew, and her past invisible. When she intercepts a distress signal in Ossuary—a language exterminated along with the colony that spoke it—she recognizes it as the tongue of her own buried childhood, and realizes the 'impossible accidents' she's been investigating were cover-ups for survivors still hiding in the debris fields. The signal's sender, an old woman named Emrys who once saved Ada's life, carries proof that the war's founding atrocity was committed by the victors, not the colonists. Delivering that message could end the war—or give both sides an excuse to finish the genocide before Ada's failing reactor counts down. In the end, Ada broadcasts the truth from inside the collapsing station, choosing memory over survival, and survives long enough to see both fleets stand down in stunned silence.
about_author: Theo Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard container ships before turning to fiction. They write about people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions, where signals fade and no one is officially responsible.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hauling insurance-certified cargo through the Meridian contested zone, Ada logs a distress burst on a frequency that shouldn't exist—in a language her instruments flag as extinct. She almost deletes it; invisibility is how she's survived ten years. Instead she archives it and lies to her crew about why. Emotional beat: the itch of a past she thought was sealed.

chapters.title: The Impossible Accident Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with flashbacks to her insurance-investigator years. Reviewing old case files, Ada finds seven 'reactor malfunctions' all within two hundred kilometers of the same debris field—the site of the Ossuary colony's destruction. The pattern is too clean to be chance. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose as coincidence becomes conspiracy.

chapters.title: Cargo Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Crew POV: engineer Yusuf notices Ada rerouting power to the long-range array and confronts her gently; pilot Sefa threatens to log it. Ada deflects, but the crew's loyalty—earned over years of shared risk—becomes the story's first test. Emotional beat: intimacy as liability; every bond is a leak.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the signal into the debris field, Ada docks with a cobbled-together habitat built from wreck hulls and meets Emrys: ninety years old, last fluent speaker of Ossuary, keeper of recordings proving the fleet—not the colonists—fired first. Emrys asks Ada to carry the message to the neutral relay at Ceres Gate. Emotional beat: recognition and guilt; Emrys knew Ada's mother.

chapters.title: What the War Was For
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV: Emrys's recorded testimony plays while Ada verifies the evidence against fleet archives she can still access. The atrocity wasn't collateral damage—it was policy, erased by the same 'accidents' Ada once signed off on. Her old reports are in the cover-up chain. Emotional beat: complicity; Ada realizes she was part of the machine.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV. The habitat's salvaged reactor—which Emrys's people cannibalized to stay alive—begins a cascade failure no one can stop. Evacuation options shrink to one: Ada's ship, which can't carry everyone. Emrys refuses to leave, saying the message dies if she does. Emotional beat: arithmetic of survival; someone must be left behind.

chapters.title: Two Flags on One Hull
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Both war fleets converge on the debris field, each believing the other is retrieving a weapon. A patrol cutter boards Ada's ship mid-loading; Sefa talks them into a standoff by claiming salvage rights, buying hours. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—Sefa protects the crew by lying, mirroring Ada's decade of silence.

chapters.title: The Relay at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. En route, Ada discovers the neutral relay's administrators have been quietly selling interception data to both fleets—there is no neutral ground. The message can't be delivered; it must be broadcast wide, unencrypted, undeniable. Emotional beat: the plan collapses into a harder, braver one.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. With the reactor minutes from detonation and both fleets weapons-hot around the debris field, Ada returns for Emrys, then uses the dying habitat's transmitter array to blast Emrys's testimony—voice, records, coordinates—on every open channel. The fleets hold fire as the truth floods their bridges. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into witness; Ada speaks Ossuary aloud for the first time since childhood.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, resolution. The station burns; Emrys dies in the debris she refused to leave, but the recording spreads faster than either fleet can suppress it. Weeks later, ceasefire talks convene with Ossuary testimony as their foundation. Ada, stripped of her license and finally visible, takes a contract hauling aid—not cargo—to the ruins. Emotional beat: grief braided with release; memory as the price and the prize of survival.
